summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a left chest portacath was admitted with acute right wrist and hip pain. She was found to have MSSA bacteremia, likely originating from her portacath. The right wrist showed signs of septic tenosynovitis, confirmed by purulence and positive cultures after surgical washout. The hip joint aspiration was negative, and MRI showed no abscess or fracture, though pain persisted. She also developed C. difficile colitis during admission, requiring oral vancomycin and metronidazole. Her portacath was retained with antibiotic locks due to difficult vascular access. Insulin was uptitrated for hyperglycemia, and she completed dialysis sessions. She improved clinically, with resolving infection and pain, and was discharged home on a six-week course of IV cefazolin, oral metronidazole, and portacath antibiotic locks, with follow-up planned.
